The '''2014–15 [[La Liga]]''' season (known as the ''Liga [[Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria|BBVA]]'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 84th season of the premier [[association football]] league in Spain. The campaign began on 23 August 2014, and concluded on 24 May 2015.

[[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] won its 23rd title on 17 May 2015 after defeating defending champions [[Atlético Madrid]] at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium]], and also equalled the all-time record goal difference of +89 (110 goals scored and 21 conceded), originally set by [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]] season. Barcelona won the title with 94 points, two more than Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/may/17/atletico-madrid-barcelona-la-liga-match-report|title=Barcelona clinch title with Lionel Messi magic against Atlético Madrid|date=17 May 2015|work=The Guardian|access-date=19 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/barcelona/11611738/Lionel-Messi-hands-Barcelona-23rd-La-Liga-title.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/barcelona/11611738/Lionel-Messi-hands-Barcelona-23rd-La-Liga-title.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Lionel Messi hands Barcelona 23rd La Liga title|date=17 May 2015|work=The Daily Telegraph|access-date=19 May 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

==Teams==
===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of 20 teams contest the league, including 17 sides from the [[2013–14 La Liga|2013–14 season]] and three promoted from the [[2013–14 Segunda División]]. This includes the two top teams ([[SD Eibar|Eibar]] and [[Real Club Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]]) from the Segunda División, and the winner of the [[2014 Segunda División play-offs|play-offs]], [[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]].

[[SD Eibar|Eibar]] became the first club from Segunda División to achieve promotion to La Liga after its 1–0 victory over [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] on 25 May 2014. Eibar made their La Liga debut in the 2014–15 season.<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en-sg/news/3882/spain/2014/05/26/4840739/eibar-seal-stunning-promotion-to-la-liga Eibar seal stunning promotion to La Liga]; Goal.com, 26 May 2014</ref>

[[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] won promotion back to La Liga after one season in Segunda División with a 1–0 victory over [[Real Jaén]] on 31 May 2014.<ref>[http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/deportivo-la-coruna/result/result-deportivo-promoted-to-la-liga_157753.html Result: Deportivo La Coruna promoted to La Liga]; SportsMole, 31 May 2014</ref>

[[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]] won the promotion play-off against [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] and returned to the top level after 42 years.<ref>{{cite news|title=Las Palmas-Cordoba La Liga play-off ends with pitch invasion|url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/138/spain/2014/06/23/4905144/las-palmas-cordoba-la-liga-play-off-ends-with-pitch-invasion|access-date=30 June 2014|publisher=Goal.com|date=23 June 2014|archive-date=2 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181002223212/http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/138/spain/2014/06/23/4905144/las-palmas-cordoba-la-liga-play-off-ends-with-pitch-invasion|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Overview==
On 2 May, Córdoba were relegated with three games left to play in the season, after losing 0–8 at home against Barcelona.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cordoba 0 Barcelona 8: Suarez nets hat-trick as hosts are relegated|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/cordoba-0-barcelona-8-suarez-nets-hat-trick-hosts-are-relegated|access-date=4 May 2015|work=[[Four Four Two]]|date=2 May 2015}}</ref> Eight days later, Villarreal confirmed sixth place and an entry into the [[UEFA Europa League]] with [[Joel Campbell]]'s winning goal against Elche.<ref>{{cite news|title=Villarreal head into Europa League|url=http://www.marca.com/en/2015/05/10/en/football/spanish_football/1431282094.html|access-date=18 May 2015|work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|date=10 May 2015}}</ref>

Barcelona, playing with a three-man attack of [[Lionel Messi]], [[Neymar]] and [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] under new manager [[Luis Enrique]],<ref name=west>{{cite news|last1=West|first1=Andy|title=Barcelona win La Liga: 10 key factors behind their revival|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32752159|access-date=18 May 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2015}}</ref> won the title on 17 May with a goal by Messi to defeat holders Atlético Madrid at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium]]. It came exactly a year after Atlético had won their league title at Barcelona's [[Camp Nou]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Atl Madrid 0–1 Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32757176|access-date=18 May 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2015}}</ref> Real Madrid secured second place on the same day as Barcelona won the title, with a 1–4 win at Espanyol.<ref>{{cite news|last1=McMath|first1=James|title=Espanyol 1–4 Real Madrid|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32757183|access-date=18 May 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2015}}</ref> In the end, Barcelona amassed 94 points, while Real Madrid finished just two points behind, with 92.

The battle for the Champions League was settled in the last ten minutes of the season. Valencia, in fourth place with 74 points, went into the last match of the season at relegation-threatened Almería, facing all three possibilities of direct qualification to the group stage of the Champions League, qualification to the play-off round, or missing out on the Champions League altogether. Valencia won the match 3–2 to secure fourth place, as Atlético Madrid, three points ahead, drew at Granada. Sevilla, with a 3–2 win at Málaga, achieved a record 76 points total without Champions League qualification, finishing fifth.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-division/match/402257/almeria-valencia/report|title=Almeria 2–3 Valencia}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-division/match/402249/granada-atletico-madrid/report|title=Granada stay up thanks to draw}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-division/match/402256/malaga-sevilla-fc/report|title=Malaga 2–3 Sevilla FC}}</ref> Sevilla however qualified for the Champions League by winning the [[2015 UEFA Europa League Final]]. 

Earlier in the season, on 7 February, Atlético Madrid achieved a 4–0 victory over city rivals Real Madrid. It was Real's biggest loss since a 5–0 loss to Barcelona in November 2010.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/planet-futbol/2015/02/10/atletico-madrid-real-rout-tactics-la-liga-simeone-ancelotti|title=Atletico Madrid finds another gear in demolition of Real Madrid|magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> 

Despite finishing the season in the 13th position, on 5 June, Elche was relegated to Segunda División due to its financial struggles.<ref name="Elche">{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/official-statement-27|title=Official statement|publisher=LFP.es|date=5 June 2015}}</ref> Newcomers [[SD Eibar|Eibar]], who finished the season in the 18th position, took Elche's place in [[2015–16 La Liga]].
